title: Neptune's Spatial Brightness Temperature Variations from the VLA and ALMA
question: Retrieve H2S, NH3, and CH4 abundance profiles across Neptune's disk from ~1 bar to ~50 bar using spatially resolved VLA and ALMA radio maps.

data.bands: ALMA 1-3 mm (including Band 6); VLA Bands Ka (0.9 cm), Ku (2.0 cm), X (3.0 cm), C (5.1 cm), S (9.7 cm)
data.sensitivity: ALMA sky RMS: 0.1-0.6 K; VLA sky RMS: 0.4-2.0 K

what.value: ALMA millimeter observations of Neptune from 2016-2017

evidence.quote: This work makes use of two primary data sets: 1) ALMA millimeter observations of Neptune taken from 2016 2017, described in Section 2 of Tollefson et al. (2019); 2) centimeter observations of Neptune taken with the upgraded VLA taken in 2015, described below.
We supplement these observations with VLA maps in 2003 from de Pater et al. (2014) in order to model Neptune’s disk-average temperature.

what.value: Voyager 2 temperature of 71.5 K at 1 bar and equatorial/polar radii

evidence.quote: Resolution at sub-observer location, assuming equatorial and polar radii of 24,766 km and 24,323 km, respectively (Lindal 1992).
Temperature profiles are calculated from deep in the atmosphere upward, assuming either a dry or wet adiabat such that the profile matches the Voyager 2 temperature of 71.5 K at 1 bar (Lindal 1992).

what.value: Temperature profile at pressures shallower than 1 bar derived from mid-infrared inversions

evidence.quote: At pressures shallower than 1 bar, the temperature profile follows that derived from mid-infrared inversions by Fletcher et al. (2014).

what.value: Protosolar elemental abundances (C/H2, N/H2, O/H2, S/H2)

evidence.quote: We use the protosolar values from Asplund et al. (2009): C/H 2 = 5.90E-4; N/H 2 = 1.48E-4; O/H 2 = 1.07E-3; S/H 2 = 2.89E-5.

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image VLA observations and construct residual maps and latitude bins
recipe.method: Flag, calibrate, self-calibrate against a limb-darkened disk model (Tb cos^k theta), and image VLA data in MIRIAD; subtract best-fit limb-darkened disks and divide Neptune into seven latitude bins.
assumptions: Equatorial and polar radii of 24,766 km and 24,323 km (Lindal 1992)
Flux density calibration uncertainty of 5% in each band

recipe.goal: Extract disk-averaged and zonally-averaged brightness temperatures
recipe.method: Sum flux density within Neptune's disk plus three model beam diameters past the limb and apply CMB correction for disk averages; average pixels within +/- 60 degrees of sub-observer longitude for latitude bands.
key_parameters: Aperture radius for disk average: disk plus 3x model beam diameter past limb
Longitude averaging window: +/- 60 degrees of sub-observer longitude

recipe.goal: Perform radiative transfer forward modeling and MCMC atmospheric retrievals for disk-average and south pole / mid-latitude regions
recipe.method: Couple Radio-BEAR radiative transfer models to emcee MCMC sampler to retrieve deep H2S, NH3, CH4 abundances, H2S relative humidity, P_mix, PH3, and H2 state for disk-averaged data and simultaneously for 90S-66S and 36S-12S.
key_parameters: PSF-scale convolution correction factor and free error parameter sigma_PSF = sigma * T * S
assumptions: Hydrostatic equilibrium and local thermodynamic equilibrium; wet or dry adiabat matching 71.5 K at 1 bar (Voyager 2) and Fletcher et al. (2014) above 1 bar
Cloud opacity is ignored; gas opacity dominated by H2S, NH3, H2O, and CIA of H2 (H2-H2, H2-He, H2-CH4)
NH4SH cloud chemistry follows Lewis (1969); aqueous solution cloud removes 5% of interior H2S and 25% of interior NH3; protosolar abundances from Asplund et al. (2009)

recipe.goal: Simultaneously retrieve latitudinal variations relative to 36S-12S and compare thermal models
recipe.method: Simultaneously fit absolute brightness temperatures in 36S-12S and temperature differences Delta T_b between 36S-12S and other latitude bands using Eq. 4, allowing H2S subsaturation or supersaturation up to P_ss, and compare wet vs dry adiabats using the Deviance Information Criterion (DIC).
key_parameters: No PH3 and fully intermediate H2 assumed at all latitudes
assumptions: Differential uncertainty sigma_Delta includes 5% of Delta T_b, sky RMS per root number of beams in each band, and sigma_PSF (Eq. 6)

not_stated_but_needed: Complete ALMA data reduction, calibration, self-calibration, and imaging parameters (inherited from Tollefson et al. 2019)
Exact MIRIAD imaging parameters for the VLA data (weighting/robustness, cell size, deconvolution algorithm, self-calibration solution intervals)
Exact prior bounds (minimum and maximum values) for all free parameters in the emcee MCMC retrievals
Exact values of the limb-darkening parameters Tb and k at each wavelength used for self-calibration and residual map subtraction
missing_for_reproduction: Tabulated zonally-averaged brightness temperatures T_b and uncertainties for each of the seven latitude bins at all VLA and ALMA frequencies (only plotted in Fig. 2, 7, 8, 9, 10; only disk-averaged T_b is tabulated in Table 2)
Exact PSF-scale multiplicative factors for each latitude bin and wavelength
Exact prior distributions and bounds for all MCMC free parameters
Scripts coupling Radio-BEAR to emcee and implementing the specific cloud/chemistry parameterizations
score_reason: Raw VLA and ALMA project codes and the core radiative transfer code (Radio-BEAR) are publicly available, and disk-averaged brightness temperatures are tabulated in Table 2; however, ALMA processing is deferred to Tollefson et al. (2019), exact zonally-averaged brightness temperatures per latitude bin are not tabulated, and MCMC prior bounds and wrapper scripts are not provided.
rediscovery_reason: Both the ALMA (2016.1.00859.S) and VLA (15A-118) datasets and the Radio-BEAR code are public, Table 2 provides a complete numeric benchmark for the disk-averaged spectrum, and the main atmospheric retrieval results are quantitative.
